cli.input: --input selects the gauge series only; default /app/data/gauge_readings.json
cli.output_dir_handling: the run clears what an earlier run left in the output directory and writes its own three files there; the directory itself is not removed and recreated, since the run does not own the path it writes into

description: Output contract for the reservoir release scheduler. Shapes, paths, field lists and sort orders only; no derivation rule lives here.

curtailment_queue.serialisation: one compact JSON object per line, trailing newline
curtailment_queue.sort: ascending by day, then reservoir_id, then right_id

field_notes.closing_storage_af: the reservoir's storage at the end of the day, never below its dead_storage_af nor above its capacity_af
field_notes.outlet_bound: true on a day whose total release equals the reservoir's outlet_limit_af_day exactly, so the outlet and not the water was the binding constraint

release_schedule.serialisation: JSON array, two-space indent, trailing newline

field_notes.curtailment_count: every curtailment the run raised, counted in full and before the cap is applied to the record
field_notes.deficit_led_service_count: the reservoir-days on which at least one right carried a deficit and so led the day's order, counted once per reservoir-day however many led
field_notes.outlet_bound_day_count: the scheduled rows whose outlet_bound is true
field_notes.reading_count: the readings in the gauge series handed to --input, counted as read and before any of them is set aside as suspect
field_notes.recorded_curtailment_count: the curtailment rows the queue actually carries, so it is curtailment_count capped at effective_max_curtailments
field_notes.reservoir_count: the distinct reservoirs the reservoir register carries
field_notes.right_count: the distinct appropriations the rights register carries
field_notes.scheduled_day_count: the reservoir-days the run scheduled, one per reservoir per day of the horizon, whatever the inflow on that day turned out to be
field_notes.total_release_af: the sum of total_release_af across every scheduled row
field_notes.total_shortfall_af: the acre-feet gone short across every curtailment raised, counted over all of them rather than only the recorded ones

summary.serialisation: JSON object, two-space indent, trailing newline

field_notes.corrected_inflow_af: derived rather than carried: the surviving sources record only the raw stage, and the board's minutes settle how a raw stage is brought onto the basin datum, so this field is computed during the rebuild and is not present on the truncated rows
field_notes.quality: `good` on a reading the basin office accepts and `suspect` on one it has marked; the governing decision for a suspect reading is in the board's minutes, not here

gauge_readings.serialisation: JSON array, two-space indent, trailing newline
gauge_readings.sort: ascending by reservoir_id, then day, then reading_id

runtime_budget_note: the scale a run is expected to handle. A graded run is killed at runtime_budget_seconds rather than timed, so a run that does not come back inside it fails on its own account and the verdict never turns on how fast the grading host happens to be

units.day: integer offset on the basin operating-season grid
